execution.coreGuidance: When executing multiple writes in a relational database, wrap them in a TRANSACTION (BEGIN/COMMIT) to preserve atomicity.

wrong.code:
await db.query("INSERT INTO users ...");
await db.query("INSERT INTO profiles ...");
wrong.explanation: If the second query fails, the user is left in an inconsistent state.

correct.explanation: Ensures that either both writes succeed or neither does.

codePatterns.detectionHint: Multiple sequential write queries without BEGIN/COMMIT

commonMistakes.mistake: Leaving database transactions uncommitted or un-rolled back in catch branches
commonMistakes.whyItHappens: Forgetting rollback statement inside the catch block.
commonMistakes.correction: Always include ROLLBACK in the catch block and ensure connection is released.

selfVerification.check: Every BEGIN block has a corresponding COMMIT and ROLLBACK path
selfVerification.howToVerify: Verify query lines and make sure error handler calls ROLLBACK.
selfVerification.failureIndicator: BEGIN query found without ROLLBACK inside catch block
selfVerification.remediation: Add a ROLLBACK statement to the database catch wrapper.

execution.coreGuidance: In document stores, always cache and reuse database client instances. Avoid calling connect() on every request handler.

wrong.explanation: Re-connects on every request, exhausting connection limits instantly.

correct.explanation: Caches the client instance globally and reuses it across requests.

codePatterns.detectionHint: MongoClient.connect inside requests or route handlers

execution.summary: Provide cache key TTL and stampede protection
execution.coreGuidance: When caching keys, always define a TTL (Time To Live). Consider cache stampede mitigation for hot keys.

commonMistakes.mistake: Caching sensitive or dynamic user data indefinitely without TTL
commonMistakes.whyItHappens: Forgetting to set expire parameters in cache client calls.
commonMistakes.correction: Ensure all SET commands include an EX option.

execution.coreGuidance: In wide-column stores, design tables strictly around queries. Avoid joins and perform denormalization to match target read shapes.
Columnar engines (e.g. ClickHouse, Snowflake) are built for large batches. NEVER write single rows concurrently; instead, buffer inserts.

commonMistakes.mistake: Direct single-row inserts from real-time events
commonMistakes.whyItHappens: Treating ClickHouse like OLTP PostgreSQL database.
commonMistakes.correction: Buffer writes in memory or use a queue (Kafka/Redis) to write 1000+ rows in batch.

execution.coreGuidance: Always ensure timeseries inserts are strictly timestamped and queried using time boundaries to utilize indexing partitions.
When indexing multiple search documents in OpenSearch/Elasticsearch, use bulk APIs (_bulk) rather than single index updates.
Ensure cosine similarity or L2 euclidean metrics are correctly configured to match the embedding model outputs.

Enforce strict HTTP method semantics: GET (safe/idempotent), POST (non-idempotent), PUT (idempotent replace), PATCH (idempotent partial update), DELETE (idempotent). Ensure proper status codes (e.g., 201 Created, 400 Bad Request, 404 Not Found).
Prefer cursor-based pagination for large datasets to avoid offset drift and performance issues. Always include `next_cursor` in the response payload.
Always use Dataloaders for batching and caching field resolutions. Never perform inline database queries inside scalar field resolvers.
Enforce query depth limiting and complexity cost analysis to prevent malicious nested queries from causing DoS.
Never rename or change the type of existing fields in Protobuf. Only add new fields with new tag numbers.
Implement ping/pong heartbeats to detect stale connections. Handle disconnections gracefully with exponential backoff reconnections.
Do not rely on the WebSocket connection for single source of truth state. Hydrate initial state via REST before opening the socket for deltas.
Store webhook event IDs and verify idempotency before processing to handle duplicate deliveries safely.
Only retry idempotent operations (GET, PUT, DELETE). Use exponential backoff with full jitter to avoid thundering herd problems.
Wrap external network calls in a circuit breaker to fail fast when downstream is degraded.
Log errors as structured JSON. Never expose raw stack traces in HTTP responses to prevent information leakage.
Be extremely careful with Singletons holding state. Prefer Transient or Request-scoped lifecycles for stateful dependencies.
Ensure trace context (e.g. W3C traceparent headers) is passed down via context when calling downstream microservices.
Queries in CQRS may return stale data. Design UI to handle eventual consistency (e.g. optimistic updates).
Every step in a Saga must have a reverse compensating action defined to revert partial state on failure.
Handle manual offset commits carefully. Do not commit an offset until the message is fully processed and persisted to your DB.
Set a strict prefetch limit on consumers to prevent overwhelming the worker node.
If a message takes longer to process than the visibility timeout, it will be delivered again. Use heartbeat extensions if necessary.
Use context only for low-frequency updates (themes, user auth). For high-frequency state, use Zustand or Redux.

commonMistakes.mistake: Wrapping full App tree in a high-frequency context provider
commonMistakes.whyItHappens: Tutorials show Context as a general state solution, ignoring React's global re-render trigger.
commonMistakes.correction: Use split contexts or Zustand stores.

execution.coreGuidance: Never mutate state directly in reducers. Use RTK/Immer properly or spread operators.
Always use granular selectors when subscribing to Zustand stores to prevent unnecessary component re-renders.
Do not sync derived state into independent signals. Use `computed` for any state that can be derived from other signals.

execution.summary: Always store JWTs in httpOnly cookies
execution.coreGuidance: Refresh tokens and access tokens should never be stored in localStorage. Store in httpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict cookies.

commonMistakes.whyItHappens: localStorage is easy to access in JavaScript; developers forget about XSS risks.
commonMistakes.correction: Use res.cookie('token', val, { httpOnly: true, secure: true })

guardrails.rule: NEVER expose refresh tokens to JavaScript (do not use localStorage or standard cookies)
guardrails.rationale: Makes tokens vulnerable to cross-site scripting (XSS) extraction.

execution.coreGuidance: NEVER interpolate string variables directly into SQL. Always use parameterized queries or the ORMs strict binding mechanisms.
Never use `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` with untrusted user input without running it through DOMPurify first.
NEVER hardcode API keys, passwords, or tokens in source code. Ensure `.env` is in `.gitignore`.
Use Argon2id or bcrypt with appropriate work factors for passwords. Never use MD5 or SHA-1 for passwords.
Always use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` when comparing HMAC signatures or tokens to prevent timing attacks.
Format unit tests using Arrange, Act, Assert blocks. Mock I/O boundaries aggressively.
For pure functions, use table-driven tests or parameterized inputs to cover edge cases exhaustively.
Run integration tests against ephemeral databases (e.g. Testcontainers) and rollback transactions after each test suite.
Avoid setting state via UI clicks. Seed database state via direct API calls before running UI assertions to reduce test flakiness.
Implement proper dependency caching in CI to speed up build times.
Use multi-stage builds to keep final image sizes small. Never run the node process as `root` user in production.
Always configure a remote backend for state (e.g. S3 + DynamoDB locking). Never commit `terraform.tfstate` to source control.
Implement probabilistic early expiration or mutex locks to prevent cache stampedes on hot keys.
Always use Streams (`fs.createReadStream`, `.pipe()`) for handling large files or payloads. Never buffer large files entirely in RAM.
Check loops fetching relations. Batch them using `IN` clauses or join eagerly to prevent N+1 queries.
Avoid mutations and side effects. Return new copies of objects/arrays rather than modifying arguments in place.
Favor composition over inheritance. Ensure subclasses can be substituted for base classes without breaking behavior (Liskov Substitution).
Event handlers must be idempotent. They may be called multiple times for the same event payload.
Favor local files or SQLite over distributed networks. Avoid heavy connection pooling.
Assume servers can die at any time. Keep node processes strictly stateless. Offload all session state to Redis/DB.
Minimize dependencies and avoid heavy initialization code in the global scope to reduce cold start times.
Always wrap `await` calls in try/catch or use `.catch()` on promises. Never leave unhandled rejections.
Use `Atomics` when interacting with `SharedArrayBuffer` to prevent race conditions across worker threads.

planning.coreGuidance: Identify the root cause, not just the symptom. Write a regression test BEFORE applying the fix to ensure it remains fixed.

execution.coreGuidance: Keep code changes strictly isolated to the bug. Do not mix refactoring with bug fixes to minimize risk.

planning.coreGuidance: Ensure new features do not break existing API contracts or require immediate client upgrades. Use feature flags if rolling out incrementally.
Ensure a solid test harness exists covering the current behavior before changing internal structures.

execution.coreGuidance: Do not alter the public API or observable behavior of the module being refactored.
